claims.head: Special teams tilt toward Detroit
claims.body: Detroit’s power play creates 8.6 expected goals per 60, 4th in the league. Montréal’s penalty kill ranks 26th.

claims.head: Point-blank against perimeter
claims.body: On shot quality, Montréal sits 2nd of 32, at the point-blank end of the scale. Detroit is 22nd, at the perimeter end.

notes.text: S. Edvinsson has not played this season. A. Johansson is in his usual spot beside M. Seider, up from third-pair minutes last season. That pair is getting 10:31 a game at 5-on-5, down from 16:09 with Edvinsson.
K. Guhle has not played this season. N. Dobson is in his usual spot beside M. Matheson. That pair is getting 9:10 a game at 5-on-5, up from 5:12 with Guhle.

O. Kapanen has not played this season. J. Slafkovský is in his usual spot beside A. Newhook and I. Demidov. That line is getting 8:55 a game at 5-on-5, up from 7:36 with Kapanen. C. Kreider has moved into Slafkovský’s old spot beside N. Suzuki and C. Caufield.
A. Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 27% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, up from 6% last season.

MTL.head: Leaning Montréal’s way
MTL.body: The two have been about even at controlling the play lately and Montréal has home ice. Not by much, though: Detroit can make it interesting if its power play gets going.

DET.head: Close, but Montréal has the slight edge
DET.body: The two have been about even at controlling the play lately and Montréal has home ice. Detroit can tip it if its power play gets going.
